trapClasses.name: Common meaning
trapClasses.description: Uses the word's most familiar sense, which does not fit this context.

trapClasses.name: Wrong connotation
trapClasses.description: Related in meaning but carries the wrong tone, strength, or nuance for the context.

trapClasses.name: Illogical in context
trapClasses.description: A real word or idea that contradicts or fails to fit the logic of the surrounding sentences.

trapClasses.name: Too narrow
trapClasses.description: Captures one detail or part of the text rather than its main idea, purpose, or structure.

trapClasses.name: Too broad
trapClasses.description: Generalizes beyond the scope of what the text addresses.

trapClasses.name: Too extreme
trapClasses.description: Overstates the text with absolute or exaggerated language the text does not support.

trapClasses.name: Out of scope
trapClasses.description: Introduces an idea, comparison, or topic the text never addresses.

trapClasses.name: Contradicts the text
trapClasses.description: States the opposite of, or something incompatible with, what the text says.

trapClasses.name: Half right
trapClasses.description: Begins accurately but includes a second element that is unsupported or wrong.

trapClasses.name: Reverses the relationship
trapClasses.description: Flips cause and effect, direction of change, or which item is greater.

trapClasses.name: Plausible but unsupported
trapClasses.description: Reasonable in the real world but not established by the text.

trapClasses.name: True but irrelevant
trapClasses.description: Accurate to the text or data but does not answer the question or bear on the claim.

trapClasses.name: Weakens instead of supports
trapClasses.description: Evidence that would undermine the claim, or that fits the opposing view.

trapClasses.name: Wrong function
trapClasses.description: Misidentifies the role a sentence or portion plays in the text.

trapClasses.name: Wrong text attribution
trapClasses.description: Assigns a view from one text to the other author, or merges the two positions.

trapClasses.name: Misreads the data
trapClasses.description: Cites a value, category, or comparison that the table or graph does not show.

trapClasses.name: Comma splice
trapClasses.description: Joins two independent clauses with only a comma.

trapClasses.name: Run-on (fused sentence)
trapClasses.description: Joins two independent clauses with no punctuation or conjunction.

trapClasses.name: Sentence fragment
trapClasses.description: Leaves a clause without a complete subject and finite verb, or cuts a dependent clause off as a sentence.

trapClasses.name: Unneeded punctuation
trapClasses.description: Inserts punctuation between essential sentence parts (subject and verb, verb and object, restrictive elements).

trapClasses.name: Colon or semicolon misuse
trapClasses.description: Uses a colon or semicolon where the grammar on one or both sides does not permit it.

trapClasses.name: Unbalanced nonessential element
trapClasses.description: Opens a nonessential element with one mark and closes it with a different mark or none.

trapClasses.name: Subject-verb agreement error
trapClasses.description: Verb number does not match its true subject, often because of an intervening noun.

trapClasses.name: Pronoun error
trapClasses.description: Pronoun disagrees in number or person with its antecedent, or has the wrong case.

trapClasses.name: Illogical tense or aspect
trapClasses.description: Verb tense or aspect conflicts with the time frame established in the passage.

trapClasses.name: Wrong verb form
trapClasses.description: Uses a nonfinite form (-ing, to-infinitive, participle) where a finite verb is required, or vice versa.

trapClasses.name: Dangling or misplaced modifier
trapClasses.description: Places a modifier so that it describes the wrong noun.

trapClasses.name: Possessive/plural confusion
trapClasses.description: Confuses plural, singular possessive, and plural possessive forms.

trapClasses.name: Wrong logical relation
trapClasses.description: Signals a relationship (contrast, cause, addition, example, sequence) that does not match how the sentences relate.

trapClasses.name: Overstated relation
trapClasses.description: Signals a stronger relationship than the text supports, such as a conclusion or causation where only addition or sequence exists.

trapClasses.name: Fails the goal
trapClasses.description: Accurately uses the notes but does not accomplish the stated rhetorical goal.

trapClasses.name: Accomplishes only part of the goal
trapClasses.description: Addresses one element of a multi-part goal (e.g., describes one study when a comparison is required).

trapClasses.name: Audience mismatch
trapClasses.description: Assumes knowledge the stated audience lacks, or omits context the audience needs.

trapClasses.name: Misuses the notes
trapClasses.description: Distorts, combines incorrectly, or adds to information in the notes.
